practice_description.medium: On-chain generative art, multi-chain digital art platform, token-based art economy
practice_description.practice_summary: fx(hash) is a generative art platform originally built on Tezos, now multi-chain (Tezos, Ethereum, Base). It enables artists to publish generative scripts that produce unique outputs at mint time, with a commons-oriented ethos, lower barriers to entry than Art Blocks, and an evolving governance model including the $FXH token and art coins.
practice_description.methodology: Artists upload generative scripts (JavaScript, GLSL, or other web technologies) that are stored on-chain. At mint time, a unique hash seed determines the output. The platform evolved from a permissionless Tezos-only model (v1) to a multi-chain architecture (v2) spanning Tezos and Ethereum. In 2025, fxhash launched the FXH Protocol on Base with art coins -- ERC-20 tokens linked to collections via bonding curves that graduate to liquidity pools owned by artists. The $FXH token enables governance and the art economy layer. Originally bootstrapped through platform fees, later raised a $5M seed round led by 1kx.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: fx(hash) demonstrates a commons-oriented approach to on-chain generative art with evolving community governance tools. Its permissionless model and multi-chain architecture show how generative art infrastructure can be open and accessible, while the $FXH token and art coins experiment with new models for art-economy relations -- directly relevant to A(DAI)'s interest in protocol design as creative practice.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes. Generative scripts produce outputs that function as standalone artworks and could serve as substrate material. The permissionless nature means a wider range of experimental work exists compared to curated platforms.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Limited for individual works, but the art coins system creates economic relationships between collections, artists, and collectors. The multi-chain architecture itself creates relational bridges between Tezos and Ethereum ecosystems.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: No for individual artworks (fixed at mint). However, the art coins system introduces a dynamic economic layer where the relationship between an artwork collection and its economic value evolves based on collector activity and bonding curve mechanics.

works.title: fx(hash) 2.0 (Multi-chain launch)
works.description: Relaunch as a multi-chain platform bridging Tezos and Ethereum, breaking down barriers between blockchain ecosystems for generative artists.
works.relevance: Demonstrates how infrastructure design decisions (which chains to support) shape artistic communities and economic possibilities. Relevant to A(DAI)'s thinking about infrastructure as a form of governance.

works.title: FXH Protocol / Art Coins
works.description: Launch of the $FXH token on Base and art coins system, where ERC-20 tokens are linked to art collections via bonding curves, creating a new on-chain art economy with artist-owned liquidity.
works.relevance: Radical experiment in protocol art -- designing economic mechanisms as creative infrastructure. The bonding curve graduation model is a form of system design that determines how art gains and distributes economic value.

works.title: fx(hash) Tezos-era permissionless collections
works.description: The original permissionless Tezos platform where any artist could publish generative work without curation board approval, producing tens of thousands of generative art projects.
works.relevance: Showed that permissionless generative art infrastructure produces a different ecosystem than curated models -- more experimental, more accessible, more chaotic. Relevant to A(DAI)'s interest in commons vs. gatekeeping models.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: fx(hash) is deeply engaged with protocol-as-art-practice. The platform's architecture -- permissionless publishing, multi-chain bridging, bonding curve art coins, token-based governance -- constitutes a creative and political design practice. Each protocol decision shapes what art gets made, who can participate, and how value flows. The founder Ciphrd is himself a generative artist who treats platform design as an extension of artistic practice.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: FXH Protocol: a multi-chain generative art platform with permissionless publishing, art coins (ERC-20 tokens on bonding curves linked to art collections), artist-owned liquidity pools, $FXH governance token, and claimdrop distribution. Also: the original Tezos-based permissionless minting infrastructure.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: fx(hash) began as a commons-oriented platform on Tezos with low fees and permissionless access. The Tezos ecosystem's proof-of-stake and self-amending governance aligned with commons values. However, the move to Ethereum/Base and the introduction of the $FXH token and VC funding ($5M seed from 1kx, Union Square Ventures, Coinbase Ventures) introduces market dynamics. Art coins create new economic structures that could either empower artists (artist-owned liquidity) or introduce speculative pressures. The tension between commons values and token economics is ongoing.

governance_model.governance_detail: Founded and initially governed by Ciphrd (solo founder/developer). Plans for community governance via DAO and $FXH governance token were articulated early and partially realized with the 2025 token launch. The claimdrop distributed tokens to existing community members. Tezos itself uses on-chain governance for protocol upgrades. Investors include Union Square Ventures, Tezos Foundation, and community DAOs (XX DAO, KRPDM DAO). Full DAO governance transition is in progress [uncertain].

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Permissionless publishing -- artists consent by uploading and publishing their scripts. Collectors consent through minting. The art coins system introduces a new consent layer: artists opt in to link their collections to ERC-20 tokens. Claimdrop distributed tokens to existing participants based on platform activity.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo artist authorship for individual generative projects. The platform itself is designed by Ciphrd and the fxhash team. Art coins create a new layer where collectors become economic stakeholders in an artist's collection, blurring the line between authorship and patronage.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Individual artworks are generated once at mint time and remain fixed. The art coins layer introduces continuous economic dynamics -- token prices on bonding curves change with buying/selling activity. Liquidity pools graduate and lock for two years, creating a durational economic structure. The platform itself continuously evolves through protocol upgrades.

data_materiality.data_sources: On-chain hash seeds, artist-written generative scripts (JavaScript, GLSL, etc.), blockchain transaction data (minting, trading, art coin activity), bonding curve parameters.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Self-generated. Scripts are authored by artists. Hash seeds are generated on-chain. Transaction data is public blockchain records. Art coin parameters are set by the protocol.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: fx(hash) does not directly engage with embedding spaces. Like Art Blocks, the generative process is algorithmic (script-based) rather than model-based. The parameter space defined by hash seeds creates an implicit output space per project.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: No. Primarily visual generative outputs, though some projects incorporate audio.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Primarily web-based. Artworks are rendered in-browser. The Tezos ecosystem has a strong culture of online galleries and community exhibitions. Some physical exhibitions through partner events and art fairs.

interoperability.composability: Moderate to high. Multi-chain architecture bridges Tezos and Ethereum ecosystems. ERC-721 and FA2 token standards enable marketplace interoperability. Art coins (ERC-20) are composable DeFi primitives. The FXH Protocol's bonding curve mechanism creates economic composability between art collections and the broader DeFi ecosystem.
interoperability.technical_openness: Platform code is partially open [uncertain]. Smart contracts are deployed on public blockchains. The multi-chain approach uses standard token interfaces. API documentation available for developers.

technical_approach.stack: Tezos blockchain (FA2 token standard), Ethereum (ERC-721), Base / Ethereum L2 (ERC-20 art coins, $FXH token), Solidity and Michelson smart contracts, bonding curve mechanics, JavaScript/GLSL for generative scripts, web browser rendering, IPFS for metadata.

network_position.scene_affiliation: Bridges the Tezos art ecosystem and the Ethereum generative art world. Connected to the broader on-chain generative art community, crypto-art DAOs (XX DAO, KRPDM DAO), and VC-backed crypto infrastructure (Union Square Ventures, Coinbase Ventures, 1kx). Strong community ties to independent generative artists who were priced out of Ethereum-first platforms.
network_position.connections: Art Blocks (fellow generative art platform, different chain and curation model), Tezos Foundation (investor and ecosystem partner), Are.na (overlapping creative practitioner community [uncertain])

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: fx(hash)'s multi-chain generative art archive and permissionless publishing model represent a significant portion of the digital art field that A(DAI) should map. The platform's experiment with art coins and token-based governance provides a case study in protocol design as creative practice. On-chain data from fxhash could feed A(DAI)'s intelligence graph with practitioner, artwork, and economic relationship data. The commons-oriented Tezos community overlaps significantly with A(DAI)'s values.
